newsitem.title: USA: Chicago policeman from troubled area held for rape.
newsitem.headline: Chicago policeman from troubled area held for rape.

text.p: A Chicago police district already under a cloud of scandal with seven officers indicted for corruption, was further disgraced on Saturday when another officer was ordered held on rape charges.
Gilberto Perez, 27, a two-year police veteran of the city's West Side Austin district, was ordered held without bond by a Cook County Court judge.

Perez was charged with raping two teenage girls, including an 18-year-old whom he allegedly forced into his car at gunpoint early Friday. She told police she witnessed Perez commit another rape of a 17-year-old in April.

Two weeks ago, seven officers assigned to the Austin district were indicted in federal court for allegedly stealing drugs and thousands of dollars in cash from undercover officers pretending to be drug dealers.

"I just throw up my hands. I can't believe we would have these kinds of people being our law enforcement officers," Leola Spann, president of the Northwest Austin Council, a community group, told the Chicago Sun-Times.
Meanwhile, Chicago Police Superintendent Matt Rodriguez named a new commander for the Austin district, John Richardson, who promised to root out corrupt officers.
